paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Hophni and Phinehas had the best seats in the house, priests at Shiloh, and they treated the LORD's offering with contempt (1 Samuel 2:17). Sacred things were right there in their hands, and they used them to fatten themselves. Being near holy things is not the same as honoring the One they belong to.

Then the LORD says it plain to Eli: "I will honor those who honor Me, but those who despise Me will be disdained" (1 Samuel 2:30). Eli had honored his sons more than the LORD (1 Samuel 2:29), and I think that's the part that hits close to home. Who gets first place in my life is a question I can't dodge, and I can't hand it off to someone else. Even a warning from a father they heard in their own house did not move them (1 Samuel 2:25). That one's heavy, friend.

But look at the little boy off to the side. While the grabbing goes on, Samuel keeps growing "in favor with the LORD and with man" (1 Samuel 2:26). And the LORD promises to raise up a faithful priest who will do whatever is in His heart and mind (1 Samuel 2:35). So the big idea is this: honor the LORD first, and He is the one who builds what lasts. The story isn't over, baker, and I'm keeping the ovens ready.
